predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: Judea around Jerusalem, with Jaffa and Gezer, whose independence Demetrius II recognised in 142 BCE (Simon Thassi page); the Acra in Jerusalem stayed a Seleucid fortress until 142/141

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: 'Judea, Samaria, and Idumea came under direct Roman administration' as the province of Judaea in 6 CE (Judaea page), with the Beersheba country as the south of Idumea; its capital was Caesarea…

rulers.name: Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II (rival claimants)
Herod Archelaus
rulers.title: Ethnarch of Judea, Samaria and Idumea

ledger.x: 142: Demetrius II grants Judea tax exemption and with it recognises its independence under Simon.
141: Simon takes the Acra, the last Seleucid fortress in Jerusalem.
134: Judea becomes a Seleucid tributary.
129: Judea stops paying tribute.
Idumea and the southern hills join Judea under John Hyrcanus.
113: Hyrcanus attacks Samaria.
110: Shechem and Mount Gerizim fall, then Samaria.
110: the Samaria campaign ends with Shechem and Gerizim destroyed; the capture of Samaria city itself is undated.
110: Medeba falls to Hyrcanus, his first conquest east of the Jordan; the page has Medeba besieged and taken after six months.
103: Aristobulus I takes the royal title and conquers Galilee.
96: Jannaeus takes Gaza.
Jannaeus's reign adds the Negev, Edom and Moab margin from the Nabataeans.
83: Jannaeus campaigns east of the Jordan.
80: Jannaeus takes Golan, Seleucia and Gamala in Gaulanitis.
80: Jannaeus takes Pella, Dium and Gerasa in Galaaditis (he destroyed Pella).
80: the eastern campaign ends with the cities taken.
The Nabataean towns go back.
63: Pompey takes Jerusalem and ends the Hasmonean kingship.
63: the coastal plain goes.
63: Hellenistic cities become autonomous.
63: Judea becomes a client of Rome.
47: Rome recognises Hyrcanus II as ethnarch. the Siege of Jerusalem page has Rome later recognising Hyrcanus as ethnarch in 47 BC; the Hasmonean page has him 'restored as ethnarch' in 47.
40: the Parthians install Antigonus as king.
40: the Roman client relation ends when the Parthians install Antigonus.
40: Antigonus is installed as king by a Parthian army.
37: Herod defeats Antigonus and ends Hasmonean rule; the Herodian client kingdom of Rome begins.
37: Herod defeats Antigonus and ends the Parthian-backed Hasmonean kingship.
37: Judea is a Roman client kingdom again under Herod.
27: the client relation passes from the Republic to the Empire.
27: Judea is a client kingdom of the Roman Empire.

c. 25: Herod founds Caesarea Maritima and makes it the capital. 'c. 25 BCE: Caesarea Maritima is built by Herod the Great, replacing Jerusalem as the capital.' The Herodian kingdom page still lists Jerusalem as capital.
The coastal plain is Herod's again.
22: Augustus gives Herod Trachonitis, Batanaea and Auranitis.
4: Herod dies and his kingdom is divided; Archelaus holds the ethnarchy of Judea, Samaria and Idumea.
4: Antipas becomes tetrarch of Galilee and Peraea, from Herod's death 'to 39 CE when he was deposed and exiled'.
4: Philip becomes tetrarch of Iturea, Trachonitis, Batanea, Gaulanitis, Auranitis and Paneas, ruling until his death in 34 CE.
6 CE: Archelaus is dismissed and the client ethnarchy is annexed.
6 CE: Augustus deposes Archelaus and Judea becomes a Roman province.

wars.name: Siege of Jerusalem by Antiochus VII
wars.outcome: Antiochus VII besieged Jerusalem for a year (from Hyrcanus's first regnal year) and imposed 3,000 talents of silver, the dismantling of the walls, Judean help in the Parthian war and renewed Seleucid recognition; after Antiochus VII's death (129 or 128, the…

wars.name: John Hyrcanus's Samaria and Transjordan campaigns
wars.outcome: Hyrcanus overran and devastated Samaria (Shechem a village, the Gerizim temple destroyed, 111-110) and took Medeba after a six-month siege in 110.

wars.name: Wars of Alexander Jannaeus with Gaza and the Nabataeans
wars.outcome: Gaza fell in 96; Obodas I ambushed Alexander near Gadara and beat him in the Golan (undated); Aretas III defeated him near Adida, after which they agreed terms (83-80); Alexander then took Golan, Seleucia, Gamala, Pella, Dium and Gerasa and later gave Moab…

wars.name: Hasmonean civil war and Pompey's capture of Jerusalem
wars.outcome: Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II contested the throne; Pompey took Jerusalem after a three-month siege in 63, restored Hyrcanus as high priest without the royal title, took Aristobulus to Rome and dismembered the kingdom (coastal plain relinquished, Decapolis…

wars.name: Parthian invasion and Herod's reconquest of Judea
wars.outcome: A Parthian army installed Antigonus as king in 40 while the Senate named Herod King of the Jews; Herod, helped by Rome, defeated Antigonus in 37 (36 per Steinmann) and ended Hasmonean rule.

wars.name: Herod's Nabataean war
wars.outcome: The Herod the Great page's timeline: '32 BCE - The Nabatean war begins, with victory one year later'; no land is named.

wars.name: Revolt after Herod's death
wars.outcome: A messianic revolt followed Herod's death and was crushed by Varus, who crucified about 2,000 rebels (Judaea page).

certainty.note: Hasmonean, Roman-settlement and Herodian frontiers are approximate: the pages name cities and regions, never boundaries.
